messages:
alex: Anyone else seeing 401s from /v1/chat when calling from a Vercel Edge app via a Service Worker on iOS Safari? Works fine in Chrome/Firefox. Repro steps below.

alex: Repro:
1) Next.js app deployed to Vercel (Edge runtime)
2) register a service worker that intercepts requests and forwards to our /api/proxy
3) on iOS Safari (15/16, iPhone) the call returns 401. Desktop Safari sometimes OK.

alex: Code (client -> service worker forward):
```js
// client.js
await fetch('/api/proxy', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
});
```

alex: Service worker handler (simplified):
```js
self.addEventListener('fetch', e => {
  if (e.request.url.endsWith('/api/proxy')) {
    e.respondWith(fetch('https://my-vercel.app/api/proxy', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: e.request.headers,
      body: e.request.body,
      credentials: 'include'
    }));
  }
});
```

alex: The serverless /api/proxy just forwards to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat with Authorization: Bearer <token>. On Safari I can see the preflight OPTIONS succeed, but the actual POST returns 401 and the response headers we get in the browser do NOT include Access-Control-Allow-Credentials; server seems to be echoing origin but not the credentials header.

support-eng: Thanks Alex — can you paste the exact SDK version and the small network trace? Also any x-request-id from the 401 response headers would help.

alex: Using @redwood/inference-js 0.14.2 (installed via CDN in the edge function). Network trace (client devtools attached to iPhone via mac):
- OPTIONS /api/proxy 204 OK
- POST /api/proxy 401
Response headers (from Safari):
```
access-control-allow-origin: https://example.app
access-control-expose-headers: x-request-id
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: r-9421a2b3
```
No Access-Control-Allow-Credentials header.

mohit: Quick thought — Service Workers + Safari are weird about credentialed requests. If the edge proxy to API issues a redirect (307/302) when using a token rotation or session endpoint, Safari can drop credentials on redirect which yields 401. Can you confirm the proxy doesn't redirect? Also show the curl of the direct call to our public API.

alex: Proxy code: it does not intentionally redirect. It fetches directly to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat. Minimal curl to reproduce from my laptop (works fine):
```
curl -v -X POST 'https://my-vercel.app/api/proxy' \
  -H 'Origin: https://example.app' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

alex: From laptop curl I get 200. From iPhone Safari it 401. So seems browser-specific.

sara: Two likely causes: 1) Access-Control-Allow-Credentials not present — browsers block access to set-cookie/credentials unless that's true. 2) If your Vercel edge function is returning Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * anywhere (even earlier) that can cause the browser to ignore credentials. Ensure the proxy echoes the origin explicitly and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.

sara: Quick server patch to try (Vercel Edge API route):
```js
export default async function handler(req, res) {
  const origin = req.headers.origin || '';
  // forward body to Redwood API
  const resp = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', {
    method: req.method,
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: await req.text()
  });
  const text = await resp.text();
  res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', origin);
  res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Credentials', 'true');
  res.setHeader('Access-Control-Expose-Headers', 'x-request-id');
  res.status(resp.status).send(text);
}
```

support-eng: Also please confirm that the service worker isn't stripping the Authorization header. When you forward e.request.headers in a SW, some clients normalize/remove certain headers. Try explicitly copying Authorization before sending.

mohit: Another angle — Vercel edge functions run on different infra; there's a known edge case where streaming or body cloning causes the fetch to be treated as a cross-origin opaque request in Safari if the SW mode isn't correct. Try adding `mode: 'cors'` and `redirect: 'manual'` to the fetch inside the service worker. Example: 
```js
fetch(target, { method: 'POST', headers: new Headers({ authorization: token }), mode: 'cors', credentials: 'include', redirect: 'manual' })
```

alex: I tried `mode: 'cors'`/`credentials: 'include'` — no change. I will try `redirect: 'manual'`.

edge-bot: deploy-notice: Deployed my-vercel@app/feat/sw-proxy 8 minutes ago (edge).

alex: After adding `redirect: 'manual'`, Safari still 401 but now the response has x-request-id r-9421a2b3-2 and I can see the edge function logged a 401 from api.redwood.ai with header `www-authenticate: Bearer realm=""` — so our proxy is NOT attaching the Authorization header when making the outgoing fetch from within the service worker/edge.

support-eng: That matches a known Safari+SW quirk where the browser will omit Authorization on cross-origin requests under some conditions. Workarounds: a) don't proxy via client service worker — call your serverless route from the page (so the browser issues a normal fetch) or b) perform the downstream call to Redwood entirely server-side (Edge API route without SW hop) or c) add a short-lived signed URL pattern so the client doesn't need Authorization header.

sara: For immediate unblock — move token usage to the serverless handler (Edge function) and call Redwood from there (server-to-server). That avoids browser credential issues entirely. We'll also create a small note in our docs about SWs and Safari.

alex: Ok I can do that. In the meantime I'll send the x-request-id values from the 401 so you can check infra logs: r-9421a2b3 and r-9421a2b3-2.

mohit: Thanks. We'll search logs for those IDs and confirm whether the Authorization header reached our API and if any redirects were seen. If we see Authorization missing from our logs, it's definitely client/proxy stripping. We'll escalate if we find server-side behavior.

support-eng: Follow-up: if you want us to triage the edge proxy behavior, please DM a small repro (repo or gist) with the exact SW + proxy code and we can run it under BrowserStack. Otherwise moving the call server-side is safest. :thumbsup:
